beats.text: One programmer broke part of the web by deleting 11 lines of code.
beats.note: On 22 March 2016, Azer Koçulu unpublished 273 packages from npm, including left-pad.

beats.name: Azer Koçulu
beats.role: Independent programmer who pulled all 273 of his npm packages after a dispute over the package name kik.

beats.context: The size of left-pad in its final version. Some outlets reported 17 lines.

beats.text: It began with a messaging app called Kik.
beats.note: Kik wanted the package name kik. npm says it followed its dispute policy, and that the unpublishing, not the dispute, caused the disruption.

beats.text: npm put the deleted version back from a backup.
beats.note: Announced at 4:05 PM and finished by 4:55 PM Pacific, about two and a half hours after failures began, according to npm.

beats.text: Eleven lines of code, and thousands of projects stopped to wait.
